description: After the fixed-factor exclusions, the conic frontier is concentrated in three explicit boundary problems: the binary cubic-factor quintic, quintic basepoint strata, and the primitive sextic conic.

independent_review.scope: No independent review is represented in this public record.

manuscript_coverage.coverage_rule: Complete coverage requires an exact LaTeX location for every program-relevant defining claim. A locator records where the current statement and evidence boundary appear; it is not a proof-review status.

members.statement: Determine whether the remaining squarefree binary-cubic leading form G3(x,y)(x^2,xy,y^2) can satisfy the Keller equations.
members.title: Exclude the Binary Quintic Cubic-Factor Overlap

members.statement: Analyze the residual degree-five fixed-factor conic branches where the basepoint lies on the fixed factor G=0.
members.title: Resolve Fixed-Factor Basepoints in Degree Five

members.statement: Determine whether a degree-six Keller map can have primitive conic highest form (A3^2,A3B3,B3^2) with no nonconstant fixed factor.
members.title: Resolve the Sextic No-Fixed-Factor Conic Stratum

members.statement: Under the stated invariant-gap and basepoint-free hypotheses, the fixed-factor conic leading-form patterns (g,e)=(1,2),(3,1) in degree five and (2,2),(4,1) in degree six cannot occur for a nonautomorphic Keller map.
members.title: Basepoint-Free Fixed-Factor Conic Strata Are Excluded in Degrees Five and Six

members.statement: For a squarefree genuinely three-variable cubic G3, no Keller jet has highest form G3(x,y,z)(x^2,xy,y^2); the surviving cubic-fixed-factor case is the binary overlap.
members.title: The Genuinely Three-Variable Quintic Cubic-Factor Stratum Is Empty

source_treatment: The linked working manuscript has exact locations for every program-relevant defining claim on this page. This says where the claims are recorded, not that they have been independently verified.
statement: Determine whether a Keller map can occur in any of the remaining conic strata: \(G(x,y)(x^2,xy,y^2)\) for a squarefree binary cubic \(G\); a degree-five fixed-factor model where every component of \(G=0\) sees constant \(A/B\); or a primitive degree-six conic leading image with no fixed factor.
title: The Degree-Five and Degree-Six Conic Frontier
